definition.name: Low-voltage LED light
definition.description: A low-voltage lighting load supplied by its driver.

terminals.label: L
terminals.purpose: Positive LED input in this low-voltage DC luminaire model. L/N are retained terminal identifiers; use the driver's +/− output pair rather than a mains supply.

terminals.label: N
terminals.purpose: Negative LED return in this low-voltage DC luminaire model. L/N are retained terminal identifiers; use the driver's +/− output pair rather than a mains supply.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The enclosure supports and separates functional parts. This original teaching model is representative equipment, not a manufacturer drawing.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: The cover limits access to internal connections. Opening it here is a virtual inspection operation.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: Metal clamps establish connections to individual conductors. The circuit engine connects terminal IDs, not the apparent proximity of 3D wires.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: Mounting hardware supports the equipment. Screws, rail clips and glands are modelled separately from electrical connections.

parts.name: Light source
parts.purpose: The bulb, LED module or emergency-light emitter converts electrical power into illumination. The visible glow follows its actual simulated operating state; heat, optical output and colour rendering are outside the electrical model.

parts.name: Electronic control board
parts.purpose: This conceptual board represents an electronic interface. The model follows stated input, output and power limits rather than reconstructing proprietary firmware.
